decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach, gradually pitch both open grippers downward toward green pepper and right wooden toy; geometry estimated from head RGB.
Finish vertical orientation and align above green pepper and brown wooden toy, retaining clearance before descent.
Descend cautiously with small image-based lateral corrections; open fingers remain above the two intended objects.
Center the right toy, close both grippers and make a short vertical test lift; retention must be checked visually.
Both objects appear retained; lift clear of the tabletop and start toward the left and right baskets without opening.
Carry retained pepper over the white left basket and wooden toy over red right basket, maintaining clearance and separate workspaces.
Replan after continuity rejection: smaller advance and lower release height to avoid full extension, retaining both objects over their assigned baskets.
Release green pepper into left basket and brown wooden toy into right basket, then retreat toward the table before the next picks.
Objects released inside assigned baskets. Use reduced retreat increments after guard rejection, then approach the two cars from above.
Approach green and yellow cars in separate workspaces; yaw open grippers to grasp across each car's width rather than its length.
Complete across-width car alignment and lower gradually to the grasp height, applying small wrist-image centering corrections.
Make final car centering adjustments without further descent, close both grippers, and perform a short retention-check lift.
Cars visually retained. Lift and stage green car on the left while bringing yellow car toward the right side of the middle basket; stagger delivery to avoid arm collision.
After right-arm guard, reduce forward increments and tilt the held cars slightly toward the basket so delivery does not require full extension; green car waits left.
Yellow car appears obstructed by the basket lip. Back up and lift the right gripper before another forward approach; hold green car stationary left of center.
Advance yellow car above the blue basket with a forward wrist tilt for reach margin; raise and stage green car on the basket's left side, keeping separation.
Yellow car is visible inside blue basket. Open and withdraw right arm while guiding retained green car over the left half of the same basket.
Both cars now visible in blue basket. Withdraw open grippers toward the remaining wooden toy and red pepper, undoing forward tilt while keeping arms on their own sides.
Return grippers to crosswise top-down orientation and descend over remaining toy and pepper. Plan central staging so objects can switch arms without crossing the arms.
Small centering corrections and a slightly deeper toy grasp, then close and test-lift both remaining objects before central staging.
Both objects retained. Move to two well-separated central staging spots, toy forward and pepper rearward, so each can be regrasped by its destination-side arm without crossing.
Lower objects onto the two central tabletop staging spots and release. Keep left EE on the left and right EE on the right; subsequent regrasp will exchange object responsibility.
Withdraw open grippers laterally into their own workspaces and lift clear, leaving the staged objects on the table before exchanging front/rear approach positions.
Move left arm toward rear pepper and right arm toward forward toy with lateral separation maintained; angle grippers toward the central objects without crossing arm workspaces.
Approach the staged objects from opposite sides of the centerline, using inward gripper tilt and separated front/rear positions while keeping each EE in its own workspace.
Align deeper over the staged toy and pepper from wrist RGB, then close the destination-side grippers; grasp remains unverified until lift.
Short vertical retention check for the exchanged grasps; pepper contact is uncertain, so defer transport until visually confirmed.
Toy is retained but pepper stayed on the table. Carry toy rightward with clearance; reopen left and lower for the sideways pepper's lower grasp height.
Left descent encountered contact; lift and rotate around the approach axis so jaws can straddle the low pepper evenly. Raise and tilt the retained toy over the right basket.
Release second wooden toy into the right basket and withdraw. Finish left jaw reorientation, then descend toward the sideways pepper with both finger tips approximately level.
Pepper shifted during approach. Lift left gripper and remove inward tilt for a fresh visual alignment; right arm begins retreat and reset after releasing both wooden toys.
Correct left approach to vertical while maintaining clearance, then reassess displaced pepper. Continue gradual right-arm return toward the recorded origin.
Recenter the left vertical gripper over the pepper's new position and lower cautiously. Finish the small remaining right-arm origin correction.
Shift left along the pepper's visible offset without further descent, close around its body, and test-lift; right arm remains at origin.
Red pepper is now visibly retained. Lift and transport it leftward toward the white basket, keeping the right arm at origin and the left grasp closed.
Guide retained red pepper over the free right half of the left basket, adding forward tilt to maintain reach margin and basket-lip clearance.
Release red pepper inside the white basket, wait briefly for separation, then retreat open left gripper; right arm stays reset.
All six objects are visible in their assigned baskets. Begin gradual left-arm return toward the recorded origin with open gripper and continuous elbow-up configuration.
Complete left-arm return toward origin and make small right-origin corrections; both grippers stay open and baskets remain undisturbed.
